- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, reduce forecasted price targets; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.  
- If model shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >75.0) following a recent dip, cap or reduce the spike to avoid overshoot; sentiment often corrects quickly.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model often overestimates; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5 units to prevent overconfidence.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after a peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect recent price mean or 10-day moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast variance; model overfits to short-term sentiment swings.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward sentiment (e.g., 0.33 or below) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.0 unit upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
